text: Topologically circular time — in which the timeline wraps around and loops back to its own beginning — is most famously associated in philosophy with which doctrine?
choices: Nietzsche's doctrine of the Eternal Return
explanation: The book links circular time to Nietzsche's Eternal Return (ewige Wiederkehr) from The Gay Science and Thus Spoke Zarathustra. Kant's antinomy (option 0) concerns whether time has a beginning; the Chronology Protection Conjecture (option 2) is Hawking's proposal that physics forbids closed timelike curves; and Belnap's branching space-times (option 3) formalize branching, not circular, time.
